steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Countries trade because of comparative advantage: each country specialises in goods where it has the lowest opportunity cost, then trades for other goods.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Benefits of trade: access to wider range of goods, lower prices through competition, larger markets for producers, spread of technology, and consumer choice.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The UK's main exports: financial services, pharmaceuticals, cars. Main imports: manufactured goods, food, fuel. Trade deficit in goods but surplus in services.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Free-trade agreements (like the EU) remove tariffs and quotas between members, increasing trade and competition. The EU was the UK's largest trading partner.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two reasons why countries trade with each other. | Describe the advantages and disadvantages of free-trade agreements such as the EU. | Evaluate whether free trade always benefits the UK economy.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Comparative advantage is about OPPORTUNITY COST, not absolute advantage. Tariffs = taxes on imports. Quotas = limits on import quantities. The UK left the EU single market in 2020 — important current context for exams.
